notes:
A short, unambiguous errand: start with Aurege, beat Varchet at dice, come back. Bullet 3 only LOCATES Varchet and bullet 4 is the thing you actually do, so they are one step. The 5 gil per roll is deliberately NOT recorded in items: gil resolves as item 65535, which is not an inventory slot the addon can count, and a requirement that can never read true would suppress the step rather than describe it -- so the cost lives in the note. Bullet 2 is the page's own '(Optional)' and names no zone; the Parade Grounds and the Victory Arch are in Northern San d'Oria, which is also the only city zone this page is categorised under, so that is the zone recorded. The sub-bullet under bullet 4 (you can still gamble after completion) is an outcome, and the whole Notes section is history -- the 2007 removal of Varchet -- except for its first line, which matters: this quest never appears in the quest log until it is already finished, so nothing in the log can ever confirm it is in progress. The page is flagged unverified and sits in Category:Information Needed; nothing in the walkthrough looked wrong for it, but no key item or item is ever held, so there is no evidence anywhere in this ladder.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: gil cannot be expressed as an inventory requirement, which is why items_partial is set

notes: Two steps on one NPC, and everything else on the page is about what the REWARD buys rather than about the quest. The '== Tonberry Hate Reset: ==' block explains the Tonberry Priest behind the blank targetable door at Temple of Uggalepih (F-11) and the 250-6,000 gil penance -- that is a service you use afterwards, not a rung, and the Priest is never visited during the quest. Bullets 3 and 4 sit under that block and are troubleshooting ('if hate is not resetting you may hold the wrong key item -- check whether Magephaud still asks for the beastcoins'); they restate the trade in bullet 2 rather than adding to it, so they are audited onto step 2 instead of becoming steps of their own. No evidence anywhere: the Tonberry key (Zilart) is the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done, and it could not have been used regardless -- 'Tonberry key' is not a unique name in res/key_items.lua and 'Tonberry key (Zilart)' is a wiki disambiguation, not a key-item name, so neither resolves. The sub-bullet on bullet 1 (you must have killed a Tonberry first) is a precondition with nothing observable behind it. Fame reads 'Outlands', which is not one of the addon's fame regions, so the region is null and only the raw string survives.

steps.note: you must have defeated a Tonberry before he will start it. The header gives no grid; the walkthrough's (I-8) is used.
all three at once. Bullets 3 and 4 are the Tonberry-hate troubleshooting note restating this same trade, not later steps.

notes: The Corsair limit break to 75. Demoted to medium for two honest defects. First, the page trades the SAME single Corsair's Testimony twice -- bullet 4 trades it to the ??? for the teleport to Talacca Cove and bullet 5 trades it again to the Rock Slab to open the battlefield -- and never says whether the first trade consumes it or whether two are needed. Both trades are recorded as the page writes them and the ambiguity is left visible rather than resolved by guessing; the testimony is evidence on step 1 only, where it is definitely obtained. Second, the start is a bare ??? with no name at all: the header is '??? - Arrapago Reef (Map 1) (H-10)' and only the Description names Qultada, who is not what you interact with, so writing him in would put a marker on the wrong entity in the wrong zone. '???' is honest and simply never draws; the Rock Slab step keeps the quest markable. Bullet 2 is a reassurance about where the previous quest leaves you, not a step, so it is audited onto the ??? step. Bullet 1's four droppers are recorded as mobs with role drop -- the page pluralises them ('Merrow Icedancers'), the singular is what a mob list shows. The RoE registration sub-bullet and the buff-wipe/Trust sub-bullets are advice. The final monster is never named on this page, so no mob is recorded for the fight. 'Treasures of Aht Urhgan' in the Fame field folds to the Aht Urhgan region, but FLevel is empty so the gate is vacuous either way.

map 1; the same ??? that Luck of the Draw uses. Bullet 2 only says Against All Odds leaves you nearby.

notes: A clean three-rung loop entirely inside Abyssea - Tahrongi, and the rare Abyssea errand where both ends are observable: the Fuel reservoir key item is granted at step 1 and is silently swapped for the Cracked fuel reservoir at the martello, which the page admits the log never tells you. Both resolve (1560 and 1562), so the ladder tracks itself the whole way. Bullets 2, 3 and 4 are one action -- find a martello, choose 'Prepare to upgrade martello', confirm, then stand where the MENU says rather than where the log says -- so they are one step; the page names no grid for any martello, only 'usually around the various Confluxes' and a pointer at the Martello page, so the step carries a zone and no grid. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a cooldown, not a step: one Refuel and Replenish or A Mightier Martello per Vana'dielian day across ALL Abyssea areas, which nothing in the packets reports. The other sub-bullets are a warning that zoning at any point destroys the key item and restarts you, and that a martello already at 100% can still be upgraded. Fame 'atah' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing, so the region is null. The reward is Cruor, so nothing here is a reward masquerading as evidence. 'Machine Outfitter (Tahrongi)' folds to 'machine outfitter' -- the wiki's parenthetical is a disambiguator and the in-game NPC is named plainly, exactly as the guide describes for Abyssea NPCs.

steps.note: near the zone entrance; choose 'Assist with upgrades'. Do not zone at any point after this or the key item is lost and you start over.

usually near a Conflux; the page lists no grids. 'Prepare to upgrade martello', confirm, then stand in the direction the MENU gives -- the log gives a different one and is wrong. One already at 100% still works.
the Cruor paid depends on which direction you completed the upgrade from

notes: The Fellowship quest that hands you the Signal Pearl. A straight five-rung ladder across three zones with nothing observable in it: no key item is ever granted, and the Signal Pearl is the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done. Bullet 1 is a precondition ('you must zone after finishing Girl in the Looking Glass'), not an action -- the same shape as A Feather in One's Cap. Bullet 6 is the closing cutscene and is audited onto the hand-in rather than made a rung of its own. The Hut Door at Ghelsba Outpost is a real clickable entity and keeps its marker; the battlefield behind it reports as Ghelsba Outpost, which is the zone recorded for the fight. Everything under the sub-bullets is battle advice -- level cap 40, soloable at 30, no Trust magic, Carrion Dragon's TP moves -- and the After-the-walkthrough Notes are entry rules (three per party, and completed players cannot re-enter), so neither is a step.

steps.note: bullet 1 is the precondition that you have zoned since Girl in the Looking Glass

notes: An Abyssea storyline quest with the same shape as the Summoner AF pages: the header's giver, Orgis, is a CUTSCENE and not a standing entity in South Gustaberg. What you actually interact with is the Cavernous Maw at (J-10) while holding a Traverser stone, so start is moved there and the header's string is kept in start.raw. That is a marker move, not a removal -- the maw is a real, uniquely named entity and the header gave no grid at all. The Traverser stone requirement is recorded even though it cannot resolve: 'Traverser stone' is not a unique name in res/key_items.lua, so the entry will be dropped in stage C and the step keeps its place without a requirement. Three rungs only. The middle one is a bare fight -- the page defers the entire spawn procedure to the Abyssea - Altepa flowchart and gives Bennu no location, so the step carries the zone and the mob and nothing else. The last rung is a zone entry: re-entering South Gustaberg through the maw plays the closing cutscene, which is why it is a travel step onto the zone rather than a hand-in to anyone. The reward table is a table of nine possible abyssites keyed to how many storyline quests you have already finished; all of them are rewards, none is evidence, and nothing in this ladder is observable at all.

steps.note: the cutscene with Orgis is what starts the quest; he is not a standing NPC in South Gustaberg
the page gives no grid and no pop procedure, only a pointer at the Abyssea - Altepa flowchart

notes: Four rungs and one genuine piece of evidence: the Mini Tuning Fork of Ice (item 1545) is granted at step 1 and is then the requirement for both trades, so it is evidence on step 1 alone. 'Summoner Level 20 or higher' is BOTH gates -- level 20 and jobs SMN. The trade back to Castilchat is marked optional deliberately: it is transport, not progress. Note 6 says a re-obtained fork gets you no teleport at all, which proves the Cloister can be reached on foot through Fei'Yin, and leaving the rung non-optional would park the mark on Castilchat for anyone who walked. The trade target is recorded as 'Protocrystal', not the walkthrough's linked 'Ice Protocrystal': the linked form is a wiki page title, this page's own Description says 'Ringing it upon the protocrystal in Fei'Yin', the sibling Trial by Ice page writes 'enter the Protocrystal' in running prose, and the corpus already keys this exact entity in this exact zone (Cloister of Frost, 203) as 'protocrystal'. If the marker ever fails, 'Ice Protocrystal' is the alternative to try. The entire After-the-walkthrough Notes section is battle advice -- Carbuncle only (Siren works but looks unintended), pet food, solo, buffs survive the cap, 15 minute limit -- plus that repeat warning; none of it is a step. There is no hand-in: killing Shiva Prime completes the quest. ADVERSARY PASS: demoted to medium, and the fight step with it. The zone carried by steps 3 and 4 is never written on this page: the walkthrough says only 'the fighting arena', the Description says 'the protocrystal in Fei'Yin', and the only occurrence of the word is Note 6's bare 'the Cloister'. 'Cloister of Frost' is read off the corpus, not off the page, which is exactly the inference hard rule 1 forbids. It is left in place rather than nulled because 'Protocrystal' is an ambiguous npc key that would be dropped without a resolved zone -- nulling it would cost the marker outright -- but nothing on the page confirms it, so neither step may claim high. A second, smaller gap: the page never says whether Castilchat hands the fork back after the transport trade, so the single fork being available again at the protocrystal is assumed rather than read, the same unresolved double-use this batch flags on Breaking the Bonds of Fate.

notes: Two rungs, and the second is a real OR: bullets 2 and 3 are not a sequence but two different things to feed the same chocobo. One Grauberg Greens pays Cruor and a chance at an Empyrean +1 hands seal and may be repeated forever; ten Woozyshrooms, fed ONE AT A TIME, instead pay the Indigo abyssite of confluence once and then she refuses to let you feed it any more. So it is one step with Grauberg Greens in items and ten Woozyshrooms in items_alt -- holding either draws the chocobo, which is exactly right. Not modelled as two rungs, because a strict ladder would demand you do the Cruor trade before the abyssite one, and the page says nothing of the sort. No evidence: the abyssite is the header's Reward, so by rule it proves the quest is over rather than that a step is done, and per-shroom progress is invisible anyway. Demoted to medium because the page cannot spell its own giver -- the header and the Description say 'Kuoh Rhel', the walkthrough says 'Kuoh Rehl' four times, and only one of them can match a live NPC. The header form is recorded, since it is the field the quest data itself supplies and the Description agrees with it. 'Chocobo' is a known ambiguous name and would be dropped without a resolved zone; Abyssea - Grauberg resolves, so the step keeps its marker. Fame 'agra' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing.

steps.note: east of Conflux #5, in the eastern part of (G-7). The walkthrough spells her 'Kuoh Rehl'; the header and Description spell her 'Kuoh Rhel', which is the form recorded.

the chocobo standing next to her. Greens come from harvesting points spread between (G-11) and (H-11) near Conflux #4, or the Auction House, and pay Cruor; the ten Woozyshrooms must be traded one at a time and pay the abyssite instead.
